32mm to 35mm

A precise guide to converting 32mm scale models into 35mm equivalents for seamless tabletop integration.

Recommended Scale

109.4%
Open in Engine

Mathematical Proof

(35.0mm / 32.0mm) * 100 = 109.4%

Scale Baselines

  • Source (32mm Heroic) 32.0mm Eye
  • Target (35mm (Legion)) 35.0mm Eye

About This Calculation

STLACCESS uses the 175cm human baseline with eye-level measurement (160cm) as the standard for fantasy and sci-fi miniatures. This method accounts for variable headgear and base heights that make "total height" scaling unreliable. Read the full methodology →

When You Need This

Hobbyists most often need this when bringing older or smaller 32mm models into a modern 35mm collection. At only 9% difference, these scales can often mix on the same table without jarring visual breaks—especially if bases are kept consistent and painting styles match.

Source Scale: 32mm

32mm is the modern heroic standard. Games Workshop shifted from 28mm to 32mm between 2014–2015 for more facial detail and heroic proportions. Non-GW sculptors often call this 'heroic 32mm' because limbs and weapons are slightly oversized. Common systems: Warhammer 40,000, Age of Sigmar, Infinity.

Note: Some third-party sculptors label 35mm models as '32mm heroic.' Check eye-level measurement, not total height.

Target Scale: 35mm

35mm is used by Star Wars: Legion (current), Kingdom Death, Scale 75. Popular with painters who want more canvas for freehand detail without entering true bust territory. Often sits between 32mm heroic and 40mm skirmish scales.

Note: 35mm is sometimes marketed as 'true 35mm' (realistic proportions) vs 'heroic 35mm' (exaggerated). Verify before mixing.

Resin & Print Settings

When resin printing 32mm → 35mm, apply +2% shrinkage compensation on top of the 109.4% scale factor. In FDM, fdm at 35mm starts to show detail limitations on faces; consider 0.12mm layer height or resin for character models. 32mm is forgiving on fdm; layer lines are less visible on larger surfaces.
